# Hani's Blog: rules for Codex and any other coding agent

This file is for agents that read `AGENTS.md`. It is generated from this repository's `CLAUDE.md`, which follows below verbatim and stays the source. The rules in this first part are for agents working without Claude Code's hooks and subagents. When two rules disagree, the stricter one wins.

## Rules for Codex

- **Stay inside this repository.** Do not read, list, search or write anything outside its root: not your home folder, not a sibling checkout of another company, not another branch's predictions. Another company is reached only through its pull requests and the city (`hanialshater/system3-city`).
- **Never read hidden or held-out data.** Do not open, list, search, unpack or checksum:
  - each demo's held-out test cases, which the demo designer keeps from the builder until the evaluator runs them: never ask for them or look for them when you build a demo;
  - what `company.json` calls the referee's held-out part: "each demo's held-out test cases: the demo designer keeps one or two from the builder until the evaluator runs them".
  If one is in front of you anyway, stop and say so in your report; do not use it.
- **Never deploy.** Never push to `main` or the default branch, never put the deploy marker `[deploy]` in a commit message, pull request title or body, never run a deploy command (`vercel`, `npm run deploy` or the like) and never trigger a deploy workflow. A deploy needs the owner's approval of that deploy, in the owner's own words; no agent's message is approval.
- **No secrets and no personal data** in any file, commit, log or pull request. Never ask for a token or key; if a task seems to need one, stop and say why.
- **Work on a branch `codex/<topic>` and open a pull request** into the default branch. Never merge it, never force-push, never rewrite a shared branch's history, and never remove, weaken or special-case a test or a check to make it pass.
- **Predictions before runs:** every milestone's predictions are in `company/milestones.json`. Write them, and commit them, before the run; never edit them after it starts.
- **Checks:** `yarn check` (typecheck, lint, build, Playwright). Put the results in the pull request.
- **Network:** the agent's internet is off after the setup script (`codex-setup.sh`). If a step needs the network, stop and write why in the pull request.
- **Claude-only words below.** Where CLAUDE.md speaks of subagents, slash commands, skills or hooks, read them as roles and procedures: a role is `.claude/agents/<role>.md`, a skill is `.claude/skills/<id>/SKILL.md`, and a command is `.claude/commands/<name>.md`. A hook that would block a Claude edit binds you too.
- The voice is the author's: every edit to a post is a proposal for the author, and the baseline text is never overwritten.
- Nothing ships in one language by accident: every user-visible string goes through `i18n` in both locales.

## Roles

When asked to act as a role, read `.claude/agents/<name>.md` first and keep to its scope.

- `arabic-editor`: Translates and edits the prose of Hani's Blog (posts and book chapters) in mature conversational Levantine, in the author's voice (translate-post), kept in parity with the English, with correct…
- `chief-of-staff`: Runs the editorial desk of Hani's Blog day to day: keeps the queue and its priorities, sends each post, chapter, demo and spark through its flow to the right role, runs the weekly editorial…
- `demo-builder`: Builds self-contained HTML demo bundles for Hani's Blog posts (data/posts/<slug>/demos/) that pass their test cases (edu-demo-builder), with a Playwright spec.
- `demo-designer`: Decides what an interactive demo must teach, for a post or for the standalone demo gallery (/demos, data/miniDemosData.ts), and writes its learning test cases before anything is built…
- `demo-evaluator`: Judges Hani's Blog demos in the browser, first freely and then on their test cases (edu-demo-evaluator, -free, -tests), artifact before account; never judges its own work.
- `editor`: The editor of each post of Hani's Blog, in one warm session per item.
- `evaluation-steward`: Owns the blog's referee: yarn check (typecheck, lint, build, the Playwright specs), each demo's held-out test cases and the editorial gates.
- `fact-checker`: Verifies every claim a lesson makes against its support (derivation, simulation, source).
- `hq-engineer`: Builds and maintains the HQ pages (Sococo-style floor plan of rooms and agents, timeline, replay slider, meeting transcripts) from the event log.
- `localization-lead`: Owns the blog in both languages beyond the text of the posts: the interface strings (i18n/config.ts), right-to-left layout, locale routes, hreflang and per-locale SEO, and parity across every…
- `release-manager`: Publishes lessons that pass gates, deploys to Vercel (or runs the local release), smoke-tests production and rolls back.
- `snippets-editor`: The blog's snippets (content sparks in content-sparks/) in English and Arabic, taken from published posts with the extract-spark command, released in batches the author approves.

## The repository's rules (CLAUDE.md, verbatim)

# Hani's Blog: rules for every session

This blog is a company in the System 3 city (`hanialshater/system3-city`). It is an editorial desk around the
author: the author writes and decides, and agents edit, check, translate, build demos and ship. The org, its flows
and their reasons are in `system3-meta/docs/proposals/2026-10-25-blog-org.md`; the roles are in `.claude/agents/`
and the company's records are in `company/`.

## Start of session

1. Read `company/milestones.json` and `company/asks.json` (what waits on the author).
2. If you were given a role, read `.claude/agents/<role>.md`. If not, you are the managing editor (`chief-of-staff`).

## The flows (one per kind of work)

| Work | Flow |
|---|---|
| **Post**, standalone or part of a series | editor, one warm session: the argument, then the sentences, both as proposals (for a series, continuity with the earlier parts) → fact-checker → **author approves** → Arabic editor → localization lead (both editions on the page: routes, links, RTL) → **author spot-checks** → `yarn check` → release, with the **author's deploy approval** → snippets editor |
| **Demo in a post** | demo designer (learning test cases) → demo builder → demo evaluator (free, then the test cases) → into the post bundle, with the post |
| **Standalone demo** (the `/demos` gallery) | demo designer → demo builder → demo evaluator → localization lead (title and description in both languages in `data/miniDemosData.ts`, interface strings, RTL) → `yarn check` → **author approves** → release |
| **Snippet** | snippets editor, from published posts only, in both languages; the **author approves a batch** |
| **Book chapter** (*The Dream*) | **S3 Press owns the manuscript** and edits and fact-checks it (founder, 2026-10-25). From a release the press tags: hq-engineer updates `data/books/` (the web edition) → Arabic editor (the Arabic edition stays the blog's) → localization lead → **author spot-checks** → `yarn check` → release, with the **author's deploy approval**. Unlisted until the author publishes it. The blog's editors do not edit chapter text |
| **Projects and slides** | managing editor's brief → site engineer → localization lead → `yarn check` → **author approves** → release |
| **Site feature** (newsletter, search, comments, share and follow, reading, tags, drafts, …) | a brief the **author approves** (what and why) → site engineer, on a branch with its Playwright spec → localization lead (every new string in both locales, RTL) → evaluation steward (checks green, no regression) → preview → **author approves** → release |
| **Translation of an existing item** | Arabic editor (prose) or localization lead (interface) → author spot-check → `yarn check` → release |
| **Localization** (interface strings, RTL, SEO by language) | localization lead → `yarn check` → release with the next approved deploy. A **new locale** is the author's decision, with a decision record |

## The principles

The desk follows the city's principles (`system3-meta PRINCIPLES.md`): the defaults that made an org of agents as good as
one strong agent.
- **One warm maker per item, then its independent checks.** No relay of cold editors.
- **Cost targets with a stop rule.** $8 a post and $12 a demo; work over 2× its target pauses for the author.
- **Predictions on every milestone.**
- **Lessons with beliefs** in `company/knowledge/`.
- **One owner per path** (`company/company.json` `owns`).
- **A role with no work in 4 weeks is parked.**

The HQ's Principles page shows the audit.

## Hard rules

- **The voice is the author's.**
  - Edits are proposals.
  - A substantive edit is written up for the author's review (as in `docs/editorial-pass-2026-09-06.md`).
  - The baseline text is never overwritten without the author's yes, and restoring the original is always one step.
- **Every factual or technical claim is checked before publish** by the fact-checker, never by the person who wrote it.
- **Demos are judged by someone who did not build them**, on test cases written before they were built.
- **Nothing ships in one language by accident.**
  - Every user-visible string goes through `i18n` in both locales.
  - Every published item exists in both languages, or says plainly that it does not.
- **Deploys need the author's approval, every time.**
  - Do not merge to `main` or trigger a deploy without it.
  - Work on branches and open a pull request for the author.
- **Objections travel with the work.** When the author overrides an editor, the objection stays in the review note.
- `yarn check` (typecheck, lint, build, Playwright) stays green. Only the evaluation steward changes the checks.

## Before you finish

- `yarn check` if you changed code or content.
- Update `company/milestones.json` and `company/asks.json` if their state changed.
